corrected_draft.title: GovInfo catalogs February 25 Covington memorandum
corrected_draft.description_short: GovInfo catalogs a February 25, 2025 memorandum concerning Covington & Burling.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On February 25, 2025, Trump issued a presidential memorandum directing agencies to suspend certain Covington & Burling clearances, terminate agency engagements where permitted by law, and review government contracts with the firm.
corrected_draft.description_long: On February 25, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a memorandum to the Secretaries of State, Defense, Energy and the Attorney General, and to the directors of OMB, National Intelligence, CIA and OPM. It directed relevant agencies to take immediate steps, consistent with law, to suspend active security clearances held by Peter Koski and Covington & Burling members, partners and employees who assisted former Special Counsel Jack Smith, pending review of their roles. It also directed agencies to terminate Covington engagements to the maximum extent permitted by law, required OPM to forward the memorandum to other clearance-granting agencies as needed, and instructed OMB to issue guidance for reviewing all government contracts with the firm. The memorandum stated that agencies should align funding decisions with administration priorities to the extent permitted by law. The White House’s published text establishes these directives; it does not establish that a review found misconduct or that every clearance or contract was actually terminated. GovInfo republishes the text but notes that an original was unavailable to it for verification. The held entry’s March 14 executive-order date and instrument are therefore inaccurate; this was a February 25 presidential memorandum.
corrected_draft.draft_limitation: The memorandum states directives; this does not establish subsequent implementation or findings of wrongdoing.

supported_facts.fact: Iran fired missiles at Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar on June 23, 2025; ABC reports U.S. and Qatari interception and no Americans harmed.

contradicted_or_unsupported_claims: Iran Retaliates with Ballistic Missiles at US Bases in Middle East

The stored chronology and casualty claims are incorrect. U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities occurred June 21-22, 2025, and Iran retaliated on June 23 against Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar; contemporaneous reporting said the attack caused no casualties. I did not find the claimed simultaneous strikes on bases in Iraq, Qatar and the UAE killing three U.S. personnel.

supported_facts: CENTCOM search result says U.S. and Qatari forces defended Al Udeid against an Iranian ballistic missile attack; Reuters result dates attack June 23, 2025 and says it targeted the Qatar base.

ABC reports Iran fired missiles targeting Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar June 23, 2025; a U.S. official said U.S. missiles were intercepted with Qatar; no Americans were harmed; Trump said 13 of 14 missiles were knocked down and one was set free. Khamenei wrote “we will not surrender.”

source_access_notes: ABC News text was directly read and supports one Iran missile attack on Al Udeid in Qatar. CENTCOM result was accessible only as a search result and its direct page returned 403. No evidence located for multiple bases.

corrected_draft.description_short: Iran fired missiles at Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar on June 23, 2025; U.S. and Qatari defenses intercepted them.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On June 23, 2025, Iran fired missiles targeting Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar after U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear sites. ABC reported U.S. and Qatari defenses intercepted the attack and no Americans were harmed. The documented target was one base.
corrected_draft.description_long: On June 23, 2025, Iran fired missiles targeting Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, the largest U.S. military base in the region, after U.S. strikes against Iranian nuclear facilities. ABC News reported that a U.S. official said the United States intercepted Iranian missiles with Qatari assistance. President Trump said 13 of 14 missiles were knocked down and one was allowed to continue because it was traveling in a nonthreatening direction; he reported no American casualties and little damage. ABC also reported that Iran’s supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, wrote after the attack that “we will not surrender.” The available reporting establishes a single retaliatory attack targeting Al Udeid. It does not substantiate the held title’s broad plural wording about attacks on multiple U.S. bases across the Middle East. The draft keeps the documented date, target and immediate response while excluding unverified additional targets or a wider missile campaign.
corrected_draft.draft_limitation: Draft reports only the sourced event; unsupported broader allegations remain excluded.
